text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore's Changi Airport is to launch a year-long shopping festival for travellers. The shopping promotion in Terminals 1 and 2 starts on September 2.
- A private dermatologist says that number of people with genital herpes is increasing in Singapore with as many as 3,500 people seeking treatement a year compared to 700 cases in 1993.

- Singapore Telecom introduced new promotional offers which undercut those of its new cellular phone competitor, MobileOne, charging only S$18 per month for the next six months compared to the normal Singapore S$40.
- Pager dealers say the price of numeric pagers fell below Singapore $100 in the past few weeks, but not due to subsidies.
- More than 10,000 customers have signed up for MobileOne mobile phone services and 2,000 people have signed up for paging services, the company said.
- Falling occupany and rising operational costs are eating into the profits of Singapore hotels but long-term prospects still look good, hoteliers and consultants say.
- A buying spree by independent oil trader Hin Leong Trading has single-handedly propped up prices in the fuel oil and diesel market, sources say.
- Singapore's F&N group is taking a 50-percent stake in a M$1 billion retail, hotel and commercial complex inside Malaysian Resources Corporation Bhd's mini-city project in Kuala Lumpur.
- The need for a pool of professional independent directors became most apparent during the latest reporting season, observers say.

- Initial public offers may be losing their glitter, going by the results of the latest two. Excel Machine Tools had a dismal trading debut yesterday, and equally, response to the public tranche of New Toyo's IPO was none too inspiring.
